newsitem.title: USA: Harnischfeger sees mining group pressured.
newsitem.headline: Harnischfeger sees mining group pressured.

text.p: Harnischfeger Industries Inc said it expects its mining group to come under pressure in the second half of the fiscal year due to a changing backlog mix at its Joy Mining Machinery unit.

"The mix of backlog at Joy Mining Machinery has become substantially more concentrated in longer delivery, lower-margin longwall roof supports and face conveyors," said Harnischfeger chief executive Jeffery Grade.
"We now believe this trend will continue through fiscal year end, and therefore, the second half of 1997 for the mining group will come under pressure," Grade said.
Chief operating officer John Hanson said the company anticipates the backlog-mix impact will be minimized by year end, with a major step-up in production at its manufacturing and service facilities.
"We are at an all-time high of service repair backlog and continue to be very optimistic about 1998," Hanson said

Harnischfeger, a maker of equipment for mining, pulp and papermaking and material handling, on Wednesday reported net sales of $794.6 million in the second quarter ended April 30, up from $739.5 million in the same quarter last year. Net income rose to $45 million from $33.6 million a year ago.
Mining equipment sales "were basically on par with last year," Harnischfeger said.
Operating profit for underground and surface mining was 24 percent higher than in the same quarter last year and operating returns improved on the quarter, the company said.

"Operating performance of the mining group in the second quarter and first six months of 1997 has exhibited strong improvement over comparable periods in 1996," Grade said. "We do note, however, that in recent months the anticipated strengthening in North American coal markets has not occurred as the mild winter reduced coal consumption."
Harnishfeger said its pulp and papermaking machinery unit, Beloit Corp, posted sales of $332.1 million in the second quarter, compared to $302.0 million a year ago.

"While our mill services aftermarket sales continue to grow, European and U.S. capital investment in mill sites is depressed by weak pulp and paper prices. We believe that the first signs of recovery are just in front of us as North American pulp prices have recently gained strength," it said.
Material handling sales were $97.1 million on the quarter, up 22 percent over the equivalent year-earlier period, the company said.
